extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers / scientists and readers of the Philosophical Transactions (17th-century experimentalists and observers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative remarks for conducting, documenting, and judging experimental and observational natural-philosophy work (astronomy, microscopy, chemistry, tanning, mechanics) as exemplified in 17th-century Philosophical Transactions summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity and duration of observations for proving Earth's motion
rubrics_metrics.description: The observations ... must be continued, to see whether in the course of one or more years the parallaxes regularly answer to the annual motion of the earth. ... when we shall have observations made in both ways, continued for a series of 20 or 30 years ... the matter will then be brought to a fair trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sustain observations over many years (decades if possible). Long-term, repeated measurements are required to establish whether measured parallaxes follow the expected annual pattern and to settle major cosmological questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of star for parallax observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr. Hook could not, in my opinion, in a better method investigate the parallaxes ... nor select for that purpose a fitter star, on account of its lustre, its proximity to the vertex, and not far from the pole of the zodiac.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose target stars that are: bright (lustre), near the zenith (proximity to the vertex), and suitably placed relative to the ecliptic/pole to maximise sensitivity to annual parallax effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument calibration and rectification for telescopic sights
rubrics_metrics.description: They can undertake no observation with their telescopic sights, till they examine and rectify them anew; in which examination there are various ways, and much room for mistake, however carefully it may be done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before using telescopic sights, perform careful examination and rectification/calibration. Be aware that many methods exist and that calibration steps can introduce significant mistakes, especially in large azimuthal quadrants, octants, and sextants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison of observational methods (telescopic vs plain sights)
rubrics_metrics.description: When we shall have observations made in both ways, continued for a series of 20 or 30 years, that is, as well those that may be made with telescopic sights, as those derived from the heavens by our plain sights; the matter will then be brought to a fair trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct parallel observing programs using different methods (telescopic and plain sights) and compare results over long timescales to assess method-dependent biases and reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record and describe comet observations in detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Father Estancel ... began to see this comet ... at 7 o'clock at night ... The tail was always directly opposite to the sun. As to the colour ... at first very splendid ... its rays were reflected from the sea to the shore ... the globe or head of it was so small and thin, that very few could discern it with the naked eye; and the father needed a telescope to see it well. ... the whole length being about 23 degrees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document date/time, apparent position and path, tail length and orientation (noting relation to the Sun), brightness evolution, colour, whether the head is resolvable with the naked eye or requires a telescope, and how the tail and bulk change over successive nights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microscopical observation reporting (structures and motions)
rubrics_metrics.description: I have observed by the microscope, that blood consists of small round globules, driven through a crystalline tumidity or water. ... I have likewise observed some of the sweet milk of cows, and find that also to be made up of small transparent globules ... the hair of an elk, and found it wholly to consist of conjoined globules ... I also observed a nail of my hand, and found it likewise to be made up of globules ... I have several times put a hungry louse upon my hand, to observe her drawing blood ... the blood passes to the fore part of the head in a fine stream ... in the breast and gut the blood is without intermission moved with great force ... these excreted particles appear like the excrement of a silk-worm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the microscope to report constituent particles and their arrangement (e.g., globules in blood, milk, hair, nail). Describe dynamic behaviours observed (flows, propulsive motions, valves), and relate microscopic structure to hypothesised growth or function. Provide repeated direct observations and careful, descriptive narration of processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental design and cautious interpretation (air compression)
rubrics_metrics.description: He took a long tube of glass, close at one end, and a plug or piston to fit it very-tight ... By pushing this plug into the tube, full of air, with much force, he was able to force it to within the 100th part of the length of the close. Whence, instead of inferring that the air was compressed into the 100th part of its space or volume, he concluded that he had forced nearly all the air, through the pores of the solid glass.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design experiments with clear apparatus and controls, but interpret results with caution: consider alternative explanations (e.g., leakage or permeation through materials) before concluding phenomena like extreme compression. Be aware of apparatus limitations and possible artefacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural reporting for chemical/volatile extraction
rubrics_metrics.description: Take in warm weather, a considerable quantity of the leaves of any vegetable, stripped or pulled from the greater stalks; lay them on a heap, pressing them pretty close together, and they will soon become very hot ... then being made into pellets, and put into a glass-retort, and distilled, they will yield ... a thick black oil ... The liquor being separated from the oil, and distilled in a tall glass body, a volatile spirit sublimes, which, after one, two or three rectifications, becomes perfectly urinous, and not to be distinguished, by smell or taste, from well-rectified spirit of hartshorn, blood, urine, or sal ammoniac.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete stepwise procedural details (materials, timing/season, preparation, apparatus like glass-retort and tall body, separation steps, number of rectifications) and sensory/chemical comparisons for product identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Descriptive and analytical reporting for unusual natural-history specimens
rubrics_metrics.description: About 200 little globular stones ... the largest being about 1/4 of an inch diameter; ... of a duskish yellow colour, and smooth. ... like seed-pearl, but more smooth, and of a perfect gold-colour ... Viewed in a microscope, they appeared very polished ... I broke one or two ... it was only a thin shell ... the inmost substance was like brown sugar-candy ... In spirit of vitriol they shrunk much and wasted, but continued their colour. Likewise aqua fortis would corrode and dissolve them tumultuously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting unusual finds, record provenance (which animal, circumstances of discovery), count and size distribution, macroscopic colour/texture, microscopy of surface and internal structure, taste/odor if recorded cautiously, and reactivity to reagents (e.g., vitriol, aqua fortis). Preserve specimens where possible and note storage conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical process guidance for tanning leather
rubrics_metrics.description: Every part of the oak-tree, of what age or growth it may be, and all oaken coppice wood, of any age or size, being cut and procured in barking time, will ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify raw material choices and timing (collect oak bark/wood in 'barking time'), and describe or provide machines/tools (e.g., machine for heating and cutting materials). Relate process steps to modern chemical understanding where applicable (presence of tannin, role of acids) and cite improvements or comparative analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criteria for papers/books (usefulness and relevance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The observations and experiments set forth in this paper, present nothing in the least degree interesting to modern chemists and mineralogists. ... A very useless and uninteresting paper. ... in one single sheet, he says, in our opinion, more to the purpose than some would have done in a large volume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess contributions by their usefulness and interest to current practitioners, novelty or relevance of content, conciseness and ability to communicate important points efficiently. Explicitly state when material is obsolete or of little use to modern readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims about mechanical advantage and hydraulic scaling require demonstration
rubrics_metrics.description: Sir Samuel Moreland undertakes to demonstrate, 1. That he will force water 60 feet high with treble the weight that shall raise it 20 feet, and so proportionably in infinitum. — 2. That by how much wider the barrel is, in which the forcer works, than the pipe through which the water is forced up, by so much is the engine pressed with unnecessary weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When making claims that challenge received opinions about scaling (e.g., forces needed to raise water to varying heights, effects of barrel vs. pipe diameter), supply demonstrations and/or experimental evidence. Specify theoretical reasoning and practical experiments to validate scaling laws and to identify inefficiencies.
